Report_ID: KOOS QOL (Knee-related Quality of Life) change at 6 months
Title: Six-week high-intensity exercise program for middle-aged patients with knee osteoarthritis: a randomized controlled trial [ISRCTN20244858]
Author: Thorstensson et al.
Comment: The paper reports change-score means and 95% CIs but no group SDs for the 6-month KOOS QOL change. Therefore Cohen's d/Hedges g and SE_diff were not calculated. M_diff was left null under the request to record only numbers stated verbatim. Six months is the paper's latest follow-up and the eligible time point closest to 12 months.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Exercise group') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); treatment SD derived from its reported mean CI; control SD derived from its reported mean CI
Study Environment: Supervised exercise sessions with follow-up assessments by a physical therapist
Participant type: Middle-aged adults with symptomatic and radiographic knee osteoarthritis
Recruitment source: Patients listed by radiologists, orthopedic surgeons, and general practitioners in the Halmstad County Hospital catchment area
Outcome measurement: Change from baseline on the KOOS knee-related Quality of Life subscale at 6 months
Outcome variable: KOOS QOL (Knee-related Quality of Life) change at 6 months
effect_direction: Higher scores indicate better quality of life; positive change favors exercise

Title: Effects of home-based resistance training and neuromuscular electrical stimulation in knee osteoarthritis: a randomized controlled trial
Author: Bruce-Brand et al.
Comment: Week 14 is 6 weeks post-intervention, not 12 months, but is the latest eligible post-intervention follow-up. Table 2 supplies common group-header Ns rather than time-specific Ns. No numerical direct RT-versus-control inferential statistic is reported. M_diff and standardized effect size were not computed because this is a three-arm repeated-measures design rather than a simple two-group design.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Resistance training (RT)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Single-centre, single-blind, prospective randomized controlled trial
Study Environment: Home-based intervention; hospital-recruited sample in the Greater Dublin area
Topic of Content: Quadriceps resistance exercise for knee osteoarthritis
interaction_type: Three home-based training sessions per week, with two weekly sessions supervised by an exercise specialist
Participant type: Adults aged 55–75 years with symptomatic moderate-to-severe knee osteoarthritis
Recruitment source: Cappagh National Orthopaedic Hospital arthroscopy database and knee arthroplasty waiting list
Outcome measurement: SF-36 physical health aggregate score; higher score indicates better health
additional_group_ns: NMES (n=10), excluded because it is neuromuscular electrical stimulation rather than the planned exercise intervention
follow_up_timepoint: early post-intervention follow-up (6 weeks to 3 months)
effect_direction: Higher scores indicate better quality of life

Title: The eficacy of strength or aerobic exercise on quality of life and knee function in patients with knee osteoarthritis. A multi-arm randomized controlled trial with 1-year followup
Author: Britt Elin Øiestad
Comment: M_diff is the paper’s baseline-adjusted mixed-linear-model mean difference, while group means/SDs are unadjusted observed 1-year descriptives. SE_diff was derived from the reported 95% CI as (14.0 - (-0.9))/3.92 = 3.8010; test_statistic was then derived as 6.5/3.8010 = 1.7105. The usual-care group is shared with the aerobic-exercise comparison.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Strength exercise') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Study Environment: Supervised by physiotherapists in primary-care physiotherapy clinics near participants’ homes
Participant type: Adults aged 35–70 years with symptomatic and radiographic knee osteoarthritis
Recruitment source: Primary care, orthopedic departments at three hospitals in the greater Oslo area, and newspaper advertisements
Outcome measurement: Patient-reported KOOS knee-related quality-of-life subscale; higher scores represent better quality of life
additional_group_ns: Aerobic exercise (stationary cycling): n=39 at 1 year for KOOS QoL; excluded from this strength-exercise comparison and extracted separately.
effect_direction: Higher scores indicate better quality of life; higher exercise-group score favors exercise

Title: A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL OF AQUATIC AND LAND-BASED EXERCISE IN PATIENTS WITH KNEE OSTEOARTHRITIS
Author: Hans Lund et al.
Comment: Table IV reports SEs, not SDs. Means are from a baseline-adjusted three-arm ANCOVA, so no raw mean difference or standardized effect was computed. The reported adjusted GMD and its CI were extracted verbatim despite the displayed mean/CI midpoint not exactly matching the reported GMD. This comparison shares the control group with the land-based comparison.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Aquatic exercise') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); treatment SD derived from its reported SE (SD = SE * sqrt(n)); control SD derived from its reported SE (SD = SE * sqrt(n))
Design Type: Single-blind three-arm randomized controlled trial with blinded assessment
Study Environment: Aquatic pool-based and land-based supervised exercise programmes; control continued usual treatment
Topic of Content: Aquatic exercise for adults with knee osteoarthritis
Recruitment source: Outpatient clinic, general practitioners via letters, and advertisements in local newspapers
Outcome measurement: KOOS knee-related quality-of-life subscale; normalized score with 100 indicating no symptoms and 0 indicating extreme symptoms
additional_group_ns: Land-based exercise: n=25 randomized and included in the intention-to-treat analysis; excluded from this aquatic-vs-control row.
follow_up_timepoint: early post-intervention follow-up (6 weeks to 3 months)
effect_direction: Higher scores indicate better quality of life; higher aquatic-exercise score favors exercise

Report_ID: KOOS quality of life (KOOS QoL), 3-month follow-up
Title: Eficacy of Exercise Intervention as Determined by the McKenzie System of Mechanical Diagnosis and Therapy for Knee Osteoarthritis: A Randomized Controlled Trial
Comment: The reported adjusted mean difference (1; 95% CI -3 to 6) follows baseline adjustment and therefore differs from the raw follow-up mean difference (34 minus 32 = 2); the reported adjusted value was retained. The exact 3-month p value was not reported (only P>.05), so p_value is null. The paper reports d, not bias-corrected Hedges g. One-year analysis was planned but not included; 3 months is the latest available analyzed follow-up.
Study Environment: Outpatient orthopaedic clinics at a tertiary health care center
interaction_type: Exercise intervention prescribed following MDT assessment versus wait-list/usual care with no study exercise intervention
Participant type: Adults with radiographically confirmed knee osteoarthritis awaiting orthopaedic care/potential total knee replacement
Recruitment source: Waiting lists of 5 orthopaedic surgeons at London Health Sciences Centre
Outcome measurement: 4-item KOOS quality-of-life subscale, self-reported and converted to a 0-to-100 scale; higher scores indicate improved quality of life
Outcome variable: KOOS quality of life (KOOS QoL), 3-month follow-up
follow_up_timepoint: early post-intervention follow-up (6 weeks to 3 months)
effect_direction: Higher scores indicate better quality of life; higher exercise-group score favors exercise
